sentence: This project studies how aging disrupts muscle stem cell quiescence and skeletal muscle regeneration through loss of methylation on a histone.
This project studies how the nervous system controls sweat gland development, to understand how skin with working sweat glands can regenerate.
This project studies how changes in DNA methylation affect gene expression from the inactive X chromosome in B cells.
This project builds computational methods that decode communication between cells in tissue and in genetic diseases.
This project studies how aging drives lung cancer evolution and how the aged alveolar niche shapes cancer cell populations.
This project studies how nuclear import receptor proteins restore normal function to a protein that aggregates in models of frontotemporal dementia.
This project studies asymptomatic tuberculosis, including how infectious it is, how it spreads, and how to detect it early with machine learning.
This project builds artificial intelligence models that use lung sounds to detect tuberculosis and lower airway abnormalities in children.
This project provides data management, bioinformatic and biostatistical analysis support to the projects and cores of a research program.
This project tries to find which genes influence bone mineral density and osteoporosis using systems genetics analysis.
This project studies which mechanical factors cause arrhythmias in mitral valve prolapse, using cardiac imaging and computational modeling.
This project develops a methodology for risk prediction and surveillance of hospital-acquired infections using federated learning across hospitals.
This project uses 3D bioprinting to make matrices and studies how cells respond to changes in shape, stiffness and chemical signals within them.
This project studies how cyclin expression is regulated after transcription to control cell division.
This project studies how cells change RNA processing, including alternative splicing, in response to changes in their environment.
This project studies how a Merkel cell polyomavirus gene is turned on and switches off viral genes that cause Merkel cell carcinoma.
This project uses mouse models and a CRISPR screening approach to study what drives macrophage differentiation and how macrophages worsen inflammatory disease.
This project compares neural precursor cells in the mouse and studies how the neurons they produce contribute to mature cortical circuitry.
This project develops optogenetic expression and stimulation techniques to control selected neural circuits in freely behaving primates.
This project uses pet store mouse cohousing to study how long-lived effector T cells are maintained and how they function.
